### Summary

A passing CUDA build does not mean every feature was exercised on the GPU. The C++ tests built on the device fixture
run on both devices. A Python test runs on CUDA only when it moves its tensors there, and most Python test files do
not. This section names the files that test on both devices, the files that test on CPU only, and two kinetics
features that the suite checks on the CPU alone: the Kessler-form evaporation and the pressure switch.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Which assertions also run on CUDA, and which run on CPU only.

**Data.** The test files and the device each one uses.

**Placement.** Read after @sec-ch13-results.

**Activation.** A Python test runs on CUDA only if it moves its tensors there.

**Guarantee / limits.** 20 of 43 Python test files name CUDA; Kessler evaporation and the pressure switch are CPU-only.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme is an inventory.

### Numerical method

No numerical method. The inventory is built in two steps:

1. Every C++ test built on `DeviceTest` ({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest >}}) runs on CPU and CUDA
   (@sec-ch13-suite).
2. A Python test file counts in this inventory when it contains the case-sensitive string `cuda`, even in a
   comment or a skipped test. Of the 43 Python test files, 20 do:
   `test_atm2d.py`, `test_cuda_workspace.py`, `test_evaporation_general.py`,
   `test_inline_svp.py`, `test_k18_contract.py`, `test_kinetics_base_units.py`,
   `test_kinetics_null_options.py`, `test_kkt_cycling_uv.py`, `test_mass_action_zero_concentration.py`,
   `test_rate_constant_ddC.py`, `test_reaction_equilibrium.py`, `test_refactor_phase1.py`,
   `test_saturation_failure_reported.py`, `test_species_registry.py`, `test_thermo_default_nucleation.py`,
   `test_thermo_none_nucleation.py`, `test_thermo_none_nucleation_after_reset.py`, `test_thermo_x_warm_start_shape.py`,
   `test_thermo_y_none_nucleation.py`, `test_warm_start_shape.py`.[^ch13-coverage-grep]

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_evaporation_kessler.py` | Kessler-form evaporation against its closed form in a box, CPU only | `rel=1e-10` | not stated in the test |
| `test_coagulation_pressure_switch.py` | switched rate against its closed form across the threshold, CPU only | `rel=1e-10` | not stated in the test |
| `test_evaporation_general.py` | evaporation rate and Jacobian, CUDA against CPU | `rtol=2e-10` (double), `3e-5` (single), `atol=1e-12` | not stated in the test |

: Device coverage of selected tests. {#tbl-ch13-device-coverage-tests}

Neither `test_evaporation_kessler.py` nor `test_coagulation_pressure_switch.py` names a device, so both run on CPU
only, on every build. Both pass on the CPU and the CUDA builds of @sec-ch13-results. No committed test or check
compares these two features between CPU and CUDA. One run outside the suite did feed their two reaction sets through
the kinetics step on both devices and found agreement at round-off. It is an **unreproduced measurement**: its script
is case-specific and is not part of kintera or of this report, so a reader cannot re-run it from what is committed.
It is recorded only as a pointer to the gap, not as evidence of CUDA correctness.[^ch13-coverage-probe]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **No suite test checks the Kessler form or the pressure switch on CUDA.** A CUDA-only regression in either would
  pass the suite. The reproducible fix is a CUDA case in each of the two test files, which does not exist at the pin.
:::

- The inventory counts a file if it contains `cuda` anywhere, including comments. Which assertions inside it run on
  CUDA is not tabulated yet. TODO.
- 23 of 43 Python test files name no CUDA device. Which of their features also run on CUDA through another test is
  not tabulated. TODO.
